assets.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Paint a landscape 1536 x 1024 location reference for the traveling fair's reviewing ring in The Goat of Honor. Canadian Group of Seven inspired oil painting with broad rhythmic opaque strokes, quiet linking passages, selective impasto, connected shadows, simplified architecture and natural warm afternoon light. The ring is a modest temporary rectangular enclosure formed by two ropes strung between ordinary wooden posts on dry grassy ground. From an oblique elevated viewpoint, show the WEST service-gate opening in the left foreground, a red tent just outside it and a small plain wooden wagon with lowered tailboard tucked behind that tent; a shaggy bay pony stands quietly harnessed to the wagon. Across the ring at the EAST side, show a red canvas awning and a few low viewing stools. Beyond, striped fair tents and a simple turning wooden fair wheel, with blue-leaved trees at the edge of the field. The space is small and practical, never a palace, arena, permanent fence, irrigation work or monumental plaza. Preserve a clear visual route from gate to wagon and enough open ground between gate and awning. A location painting with no named actors and no plot action, no labels or text, no magical glowing props. The style reference is only for oil brushwork and organization of light; entirely new fair setting.

Use case: illustration-story. Create a literary comic-fantasy book cover, portrait 864 x 1536, 9:16. Exact title once, clearly readable: The Goat of Honor. Place the title in confident cream serif lettering across the upper sky with generous margins. Foreground: Hobnob, a grey ordinary goat with a cream beard, crooked LEFT horn and irregular white left-flank patch, regards the viewer with patient stubbornness beside a small gold-painted pasteboard crown. A youthful adult newcomer in a grey modern hoodie, red trainers and a green long tabard embroidered with little crowned turnips stands beside a wooden performer's wagon farther back; his costume neckline is comically torn, his posture is wary rather than heroic. His hood can be down; no long beard attached to him. A few striped fair tents, a red awning, and blue-leaved trees recede behind them in warm afternoon daylight. Compose a novel cover around goat, costume and the small promise of shelter, with one inviting visual tension rather than an illustrated plot summary. Canadian Group of Seven inspired oil paint: broad rhythmic colour/value shapes, varied opaque strokes, simplified figures, subtle impasto, joined shadows and lost edges, natural motivated light. Soft cream, grey, muted red and greens with the story's blue foliage; avoid automatic orange-blue contrast, glossy faces, rim lighting, weapons, violence, or distressed animals. The goat-sheet reference defines Hobnob's identity only; the orchard reference defines painterly style only. Do not reproduce reference labels or orchard scene.
